slides.title: Compile-Time Computation
slides.prompt: Template Metaprogramming (TMP) executes logic at compile time. Modern C++ simplifies TMP using `constexpr`, `consteval`, and `if constexpr`.

slides.title: Compile-Time If Branching Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the C++17 keyword for compile-time conditional branching.

slides.title: if constexpr Advantage over standard if
slides.prompt: What is the primary benefit of 'if constexpr' over a regular 'if' statement inside a template function?
options: Discarded branches are not instantiated by the compiler, avoiding compilation errors for invalid sub-type operations
Allows dynamically changing variable types inside main()
Disables exception throwing inside both branches
slides.correctAnswer: Discarded branches are not instantiated by the compiler, avoiding compilation errors for invalid sub-type operations

slides.title: Consteval Keyword C++20
slides.prompt: C++20 introduced ___ for immediate functions that MUST execute at compile time.
slides.codeSnippet: ___ int getSquare(int x) { return x * x; }

slides.title: constexpr vs consteval Difference
slides.prompt: How does 'consteval' differ from 'constexpr' in C++20?
options: 'consteval' guarantees function execution at compile-time only (fails if invoked with runtime values); 'constexpr' can run at runtime or compile-time
'constexpr' works only for templates; 'consteval' works only for void functions
slides.correctAnswer: 'consteval' guarantees function execution at compile-time only (fails if invoked with runtime values); 'constexpr' can run at runtime or compile-time

slides.title: Static Assert Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to perform compile-time assertion testing.

slides.title: constinit Keyword C++20
slides.prompt: What does the C++20 'constinit' keyword guarantee for a variable?
options: Guarantees the variable is initialized at compile time (prevents static initialization order fiasco), but permits runtime mutation if non-const
Forces the variable to be read-only constant throughout runtime
Forces function parameters to be initialized to zero
slides.correctAnswer: Guarantees the variable is initialized at compile time (prevents static initialization order fiasco), but permits runtime mutation if non-const

slides.title: Type Traits Value Extraction
slides.prompt: In struct Meta-functions, compile-time return values were traditionally passed via static constexpr ___ value.

slides.title: Template Metaprogramming Drawback
slides.prompt: What is a well-known drawback of extensive traditional Template Metaprogramming?
options: Increased compilation times and cryptic compiler error messages
Significant runtime CPU overhead and slow execution
slides.correctAnswer: Increased compilation times and cryptic compiler error messages
